thread:
maya: Quick note: PTQ canary for raven-lite-ptq-rc1 shows elevated structured-output parse failures for funcalls vs FP16 baseline. Not huge but consistent.

maya: Summary numbers from 50k canary requests: FP16 parse success 98.9% -> PTQ 92.8%.

sahil: yikes. do you have raw examples of failures? truncated vs syntax noise?

maya: pasted two representative snippets from raw assistant tokens: 

```
assistant: {"tool": "search", "args": {"query": "best espresso 2026"}}
assistant: {"tool": "search", "args": {"query": "best espresso 2026"}
# missing final brace, cut mid-object
```

```
assistant: {"tool": "summarize", "args": {"items": ["x","y",]}}
# trailing comma in array -> invalid JSON
```

jess: looks punctuation/trailing-char related. do we see any pattern with long arrays or nested maps?

maya: breakdown by failure mode: truncated: 3.9% | small-syntax: 3.3% | other noise: 0.0% (rounded). FP16 truncated ~0.5%, small-syntax ~0.6%

owen: confirm decode settings identical between runs? temp/top_p/stop tokens?

maya: yes, decode args same across runs: temperature=0.0, top_p=0.95, max_tokens=256, stop=["\n\n"]

eva: we re-ran a small sample with top_p disabled (greedy) and saw parse_success improve by ~0.8% but not fully close the gap.

sahil: hypothesis: PTQ shifts token probs near punctuation boundaries causing the model to either emit an extra delimiter or stop earlier. that explains both truncated and stray commas. two mitigation paths: 1) server-side lightweight repair step (repair common patterns) 2) prompt/decoder adjustments or sentinel wrapper to force proper termination.

jess: we already have parser_repair in parsing_lib that handles trailing commas and missing final braces by simple heuristics. but repairs are not perfect and could mask real semantic issues. prefer combining sentinel token + repair as a staged defense.

maya: proposed experiment matrix: vary temp (0.0, 0.08, 0.16), toggle top_p, enable parser_repair, add closing sentinel token ("</JSON>") in prompt, flip a kernel variant on 10% hosts labeled "decode-tiling-fix". run 10k samples per condition.

owen: for canary routing, recommend quick fallback: if tenant-level parse_success < 95% for 5min, route to FP16 pool for that tenant and fire an alert. keeps customer threads healthy.

eva: scheduled canary job id=1729908801 for the matrix. samples=10000 per condition. will push logs here. tagging ops to be ready for fallback triggers.

canary-bot: canary job 1729908801 started: model=raven-lite-ptq-rc1 conditions=[temp0.0,temp0.08,temp0.16,top_p_off,parser_repair_on,sentinel_on,kernel_flip_10pct] samples=10000 each.

maya: reproduction snippet for local devs: 

```
# python psuedo-repro
prompts = [
  "Run tool call and output JSON: search(query=\"best espresso 2026\")",
  "Run tool call and return JSON: summarize(items=[\"a\",\"b\"])"
]
for p in prompts:
  call_model(endpoint, prompt=p, decode={"temperature":0.0, "top_p":0.95, "max_tokens":256})
  save_raw_tokens()
```

jess: I'll run local tests: enable parser_repair locally, try sentinel wrapper, and measure parse lift on 200 adversarial prompts. will report.

sahil: I'll flip kernel variant on a small host subset and compare raw token streams to baseline; log any token-prob shifts we can measure.

owen: I'll draft fallback routing rule and the escalation runbook: automatic route-to-FP16, notify oncall, and block auto-promotion until parse_success >= 95% for 30m.

maya: notes: semantic evals (QA metrics/ROUGE) show no degradation vs FP16 in the sampled set, so issue is structural not semantic. good to know.

eva: initial partial results: parser_repair recovers ~1.8% of errors; sentinel wrapper recovers ~2.6%; combined gets us closer but still ~1% shy of baseline in worst condition. will post full table when job completes.

canary-bot: canary job 1729908801 partial update: temp=0.0 parse_success=92.7%, temp=0.08 parse_success=93.4%, sentinel_on parse_success=95.1% (10000 samples each). full report pending.
